title: Sampling means and the CLT
intro: Use the spread of sample means, not the spread of individual values.

beats.spoken: We want an average, not one observation. Independent population readings have mean eighty and standard deviation twelve.
beats.coach: Find a probability about X̄, an average of 36 independent readings, not about one reading. Population μ = 80 and σ = 12.

beats.spoken: The sample mean keeps the same centre. Its spread is the standard error: twelve divided by the square root of thirty-six.
beats.coach: The sample mean keeps centre 80. Its standard error is 12/√36 = 2.

beats.spoken: For this large sample, the CLT gives an approximately normal mean. A normal population would give an exact normal mean.
beats.coach: The distribution of the mean is approximately normal here. For a normal population, the distribution of the mean is exactly normal.

beats.spoken: On a Calculator page, open Probability, Distributions, then Normal Cdf.
beats.coach: On a Calculator page: Menu → 5 Probability → 5 Distributions → 2 Normal Cdf.

beats.spoken: Enter the lower and upper bounds of the interval.
beats.coach: Lower Bound 78, Upper Bound 83. Each Tab moves the highlight to the next field.

beats.spoken: Keep the mean at eighty. Enter two as the standard deviation of the mean, not twelve and not the variance four.
beats.coach: Enter μ = 80 and σ = 2. Normal Cdf wants a standard deviation: do not enter 12 or the variance 4.

beats.spoken: Enter inserts the command, then Enter again evaluates it.
beats.coach: First Enter inserts normCdf(78,83,80,2). The second Enter evaluates the command.

beats.spoken: The chance is about zero point seven seven five under the normal approximation. Distinguish an exact normal model from an approximation.
beats.coach: P(78 < X̄ < 83) ≈ 0.775 under the normal approximation. Keep the normality assumption with the result.
